title: Rajnath Singh Represents India at SCO Heads of Government Meeting in Dushanbe
excerpt: India's defence minister met Tajik Prime Minister Qohir Rosulzoda and Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref in Dushanbe, and used his SCO address to call for an end to double standards on terrorism.
body:
• Defence Minister Rajnath Singh is representing India at the 25th meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of Government in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 19-20.
  • Singh met Tajik Prime Minister Qohir Rosulzoda on October 20, stressing longstanding civilisational ties and deep people-to-people links between India and Tajikistan, and also met Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref.
  • In his address, Singh said terrorism harms innocent lives and disrupts investment and commerce, and called for the entire ecosystem of terrorism to be eliminated with no double standards.
  • The meeting focuses on trade, economy, investment, connectivity, innovation and cultural-humanitarian exchanges, and will review the SCO's financial and institutional functioning.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met Tajikistan Prime Minister Qohir Rosulzoda in Dushanbe on Tuesday, October 20, as he represented India at the meeting of the Council of Heads of Government of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), according to The Hindu. Singh said he underlined the longstanding civilisational ties and deep people-to-people links between India and Tajikistan in the meeting, which came at the commencement of the two-day gathering in the Tajik capital.

Singh is in Tajikistan on a two-day official visit for the 25th meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of Government. He was accorded a ceremonial welcome on his arrival at Dushanbe airport on October 19, where he was greeted by Tajikistan's Defence Minister Emomali Sobirzoda and Sherali Jonon of the country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Bilateral Meetings on the Sidelines

Beyond the plenary sessions, Singh used the visit for a series of bilateral engagements. He met Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref on the sidelines of the meeting, IANS reported. "Pleasure to meet H.E. Mr Mohammad Reza Aref, First Vice President of Iran on the sidelines of the SCO Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe," Singh wrote on X after the meeting.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=5pml8US3Qkk

A day earlier, Singh held talks with Tajik Defence Minister Emomali Sobirzoda. "Had a productive discussion with Defence Minister of Tajikistan in Dushanbe on the sidelines of the SCO Heads of Government Meeting. We exchanged views on strengthening bilateral defence cooperation in areas of mutual interest with emphasis on capacity building and training," he posted on X.

A Call to End Double Standards on Terrorism

In his address to the Council of Heads of Government, Singh placed counter-terrorism at the centre of India's message. Terrorism, he said, remains one of the most serious threats to peace and development, harming innocent lives while disrupting investment and commerce, radicalising societies and depriving young people of opportunities.

https://x.com/rajnathsingh/status/2112416283333701890

"There can be no justification for terrorism. There can be no double standards in dealing with it, and there can be no place for those who finance, support, or provide safe haven to terrorists. The entire ecosystem of terrorism must be firmly and collectively eliminated."

— Rajnath Singh, India's Defence Minister

Singh recalled Prime Minister Narendra Modi's remarks at the SCO summit in Bishkek, where Modi set out India's vision for the organisation based on security, connectivity and opportunity. That message, Singh said, is particularly relevant for the Council of Heads of Government, the SCO body that handles the bloc's economic and institutional agenda.

What the Dushanbe Meeting Will Decide

The Council of Heads of Government meeting will focus on strengthening multilateral cooperation among SCO member states, particularly in trade, economy, investment, connectivity, innovation and cultural-humanitarian exchanges, according to a press release by India's Ministry of External Affairs cited by The Hindu. The meeting is also expected to review the progress of ongoing cooperation initiatives and consider decisions relating to the organisation's financial and institutional functioning.

India remains actively engaged across SCO mechanisms, contributing through initiatives in startups and innovation, digital public infrastructure and people-to-people exchanges. The SCO has 10 member states — India, Belarus, Iran, Kazakhstan, China, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan — along with two observer states and 15 dialogue partners, according to the Ministry of Defence statement reported by IANS.

Why It Matters

The Dushanbe meeting is the 25th edition of the Council of Heads of Government. The previous meeting was held in Moscow on November 18, 2025, where India was represented by External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar. New Delhi's decision to send its defence minister this year underlines the breadth of India's engagement with the Eurasian bloc at a time when connectivity, trade routes and regional security are being renegotiated across Central Asia. For India, Tajikistan is a long-standing partner in that region, and Singh's meetings in Dushanbe paired the multilateral agenda with direct bilateral outreach on defence training and capacity building.

Decisions taken in Dushanbe on the SCO's financial and institutional functioning, and on the next phase of its trade and connectivity initiatives, will shape how much practical weight the bloc carries into its next summit cycle.
